root.name: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit Declined: Brombacher Countergambit
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. f3 c5

overview: After 4.f3 Black counters with 4...c5, striking at d4 instead of defending e4. White can push d5 or play fxe4 and take on c5 with an open game. It is a sharp, tactical line for both sides.

white_ideas.idea: Take on e4 and recapture quickly
Use the lead in development with Bc4 and Nge2
Central play with d5 or dxc5

black_ideas.idea: Keep the extra pawn if possible

typical_structures.structure: Open centre; Black pawn on c5 against d4

gambit.notes: White is a pawn down after 3...dxe4 unless he regains it.

character.reason: The countergambit leads to open, tactical play.

gambit.reason: White is a pawn down and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: White's compensation is generally considered insufficient.

approach.reason: Strong players hardly ever choose the BDG.

plans.reason: White plays for development and attack.
